transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I guess... I’ve just been feeling low for a long time. I still do my routes and my volunteer shifts, but most days it feels heavy, like I’m just going through the motions.
Do you still find pleasure in the things you used to enjoy, like your volunteer work?
I don’t know… I still show up for it. Some days it feels alright, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I get much out of it like I used to.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?
Not really sure. I mean, I still do a few things, but I wouldn’t say I really look forward to them much.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
Yeah… I guess maybe some. I still do things, but it’s hard to say I really enjoy them the way I used to.
Do you feel sad most of the day?
Yeah… most days, I’d say. I can get through my routes and the volunteer stuff, but there’s this low, heavy feeling there a lot of the time. Like I’m just going through the motions.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?
Not really… I don’t keep close track, but my clothes seem about the same.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Some, yeah. Mostly before a run… I’ll lie there thinking about the next day’s stops, or I wake up around four and don’t really get back to sleep. I still get to work, but I feel pretty worn out starting the day.
How long have you been feeling this low and heavy?
About three years, I guess… since my father died. It’s just kind of stayed with me since then.
Have you experienced any periods of even worse depression during these three years?

I don’t know if I’d call it “even worse” in stretches. It’s more like… most days there’s just this heavy, low feeling sitting there. I still do my routes and the volunteer stuff, but a lot of the time I’m just going through the motions.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide?
Not really… I mean, I get tired of feeling this way, but I haven’t been sitting around planning anything like that.
Have you had any periods where you felt like you couldn't take care of yourself or your daily responsibilities?

Not like I stopped completely, no. I still get to work, and I still go to the pantry. It just… takes more pushing than it used to. And I’ve had this logistics supervisor application sitting there unfinished, because I don’t really trust myself to keep up with it.
Have you had any periods in the last three years where you felt completely unable to get out of bed or leave your house?

No… not completely. I mean, I get out and I show up for work, and I still go to the pantry. It just takes more pushing than it used to. Some things I’ve let sit, like that supervisor application… I just don’t really trust myself to keep up with it.
Have you had any periods in the last three years where your depression was so severe that you felt like you were unable to function at all?

No, not unable to function at all. I’m still showing up for work, still going to the pantry and that. It’s just… everything takes more pushing than it used to. I’ve let some things sit, like that supervisor application, because I don’t really trust myself to keep up with it.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now feel completely uninterested in?
I’m not sure… nothing comes to mind as completely uninterested. I still do things, just maybe not with much excitement.
Have you had any periods in the last three years where you felt completely overwhelmed by your depression?

Yeah… I guess overwhelmed in a quiet way. Not like I stop everything, but most days there’s this heavy, low feeling on me. I still get through my routes and the volunteer shifts, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
Would you say that your low, heavy feeling most days is mild, moderate, or severe?
I’d say mild. It’s there most days, that heavy, low feeling, but I still get through my routes and the volunteer shifts. Just feels like I’m going through the motions a lot of the time.
Would you describe the heavy, low feeling you've been experiencing most days as persistent but not usually interfering with your daily activities?
Yeah… that’s probably right. It’s there most days, this heavy, low feeling, but I still get my routes done and show up for the volunteer shifts. I just feel like I’m going through the motions a lot.
